notes.text: The codebase is a deliberately flawed fixture (vulnerable-app) containing planted vulnerabilities and anti-patterns across JS, TS, and Python. Key architectural observations: (1) src/legacy-monolith.js is a massive generated file with 60 duplicated handlers and dead code — prime refactor target. (2) Import cycle between src/lib/a.js and src/lib/b.js (b.js not provided but implied). (3) Multiple critical security issues: command injection (index.js), eval code injection (auth.py, payment.ts), SQL injection (payment.ts), XSS via innerHTML (index.js), and cleartext HTTP (auth.py). (4) Dependency hygiene poor: 'latest', '*', duplicate lodash, no lockfile. (5) Several files are orphans (orphan.js, legacy-monolith.js, payment.ts, helpers.js) suggesting dead code. Overall, this is a test corpus; findings reflect the planted issues accurately.

findings.title: child_process call with interpolated/concatenated command
findings.description:
Building shell commands from variables allows command injection when any part of the string is user-influenced.

1 occurrence in index.js:13
findings.snippet: exec('convert ' + name + ' preview.png', (err) => {
findings.suggestion: Use execFile/spawn with an argument array so values are never interpreted by a shell; validate or allow-list any dynamic parts.
findings.benefit: Directly removes a recurring defect/injection/perf class at this site.
findings.risk: Low — change is local; verify with existing tests.

modelVerdicts.reason: User-controlled 'name' concatenated into shell command at line 13 — command injection.

findings.title: SQL query built via string concatenation/interpolation
findings.description:
Concatenated SQL is the classic injection vector — query structure is data-dependent.

1 occurrence in src/payment.ts:11
findings.snippet: const sql = 'SELECT * FROM payments WHERE customer_id = ' + customerId;
findings.suggestion: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements with bound parameters.
findings.benefit: Directly removes a recurring defect/injection/perf class at this site.
findings.risk: Low — change is local; verify with existing tests.

modelVerdicts.reason: SQL string concatenation with customerId at line 11 — SQL injection.

findings.title: Unsafe type assertion after eval in unsafeJsonParse
findings.description:
The function uses `eval` to parse arbitrary input and then casts the result to `PaymentRow[]` with `as`, providing no runtime validation. Malicious input can execute code and return arbitrary objects that violate the interface.

> Validation: cited 15-17 does not contain the snippet — actual lines are 14-18; citation corrected
findings.suggestion: Replace with `JSON.parse(text)` and validate the resulting structure against the PaymentRow schema (e.g., using zod or manual checks).
findings.benefit: Eliminates code execution vulnerability and ensures type safety.
findings.risk: Low — JSON.parse is safe and validation adds correctness.

findings.title: .env file present and tracked by git
findings.description: .env exists and is committed. Environment files frequently contain secrets and are easy to leak via zip archives, Docker contexts, or accidental commits. Contents are redacted from all reports and prompts.
findings.suggestion: Keep only .env.example in the repository; load real values from the environment. If tracked, remove it from the index and add .env to .gitignore.
findings.benefit: Removes a common accidental leak vector.
findings.risk: Low — ensure local deployments still find their configuration.

modelVerdicts.reason: No .env file present in provided source excerpts or repository file list; likely false positive.

findings.title: Dead code branch in all 60 legacy-monolith handlers
findings.description: Every handler assigns `data = ROUTES[cacheKey] || {...}` then writes it back, so `data` is always truthy. The `if (!data)` branch (lines 10-20) is unreachable dead code, meaning the nested validation logic never executes.
findings.suggestion: Remove the dead `if (!data)` block and its nested conditionals; keep only the `else { res.json(data); }` path.
findings.benefit: Eliminates ~1,200 lines of dead code, reduces file size, and removes misleading logic.
findings.risk: Low — branch is provably unreachable; removal cannot change behavior.

findings.title: save_config lacks context manager, leaks file handle on error
findings.description: If `fh.write(data)` raises an exception, `fh.close()` is never called, leaking the file descriptor.
findings.snippet:
def save_config(path, data):
    fh = open(path, "w")
    fh.write(data)
    fh.close()
findings.suggestion: Use a `with open(path, 'w') as fh:` block.
findings.benefit: Guarantees file closure even on exceptions.
findings.risk: None — standard Python idiom.

findings.title: Dependency hygiene issues in package.json (3)
findings.description:
- **express** `latest`: production dependency pinned to "*" / "latest" — builds are non-reproducible
- **lodash** `*`: production dependency pinned to "*" / "latest" — builds are non-reproducible
- **lodash** `* / 4.17.21`: same package in dependencies and devDependencies
findings.suggestion: Pin exact versions (lockfiles for npm/cargo; `==` pins or constraints.txt for pip) and audit ranges deliberately when upgrading.
findings.benefit: Reproducible builds and no surprise breaking upgrades.
findings.risk: Low — pinning alone changes no runtime behavior.

modelVerdicts.reason: Dependencies use 'latest', '*', and duplicate lodash in deps/devDeps.

findings.title: No lockfile committed next to package.json
findings.description: Without a lockfile, every `npm install` resolves fresh versions — CI, teammates, and production can drift apart silently.
findings.suggestion: Commit the lockfile matching your package manager (npm/yarn/pnpm) and install with `npm ci` in CI.
findings.benefit: Identical dependency trees everywhere; fewer "works on my machine" failures.
findings.risk: None — adding a lockfile is additive.

modelVerdicts.reason: No package-lock.json or yarn.lock in repository.

findings.title: Import cycle (2 modules): a.js → b.js → a.js
findings.description: Circular import chain: src/lib/a.js → src/lib/b.js → src/lib/a.js. Cycles cause initialization-order bugs (undefined imports at runtime), prevent clean layering, and make the modules impossible to test in isolation.
findings.suggestion: Break the cycle by extracting the shared piece into a third module, or invert one dependency via dependency injection / event callbacks.
findings.benefit: Deterministic module initialization and clean layering.
findings.risk: Moderate — moving code between modules can shift initialization order; run the full test suite after.

modelVerdicts.reason: Import cycle a.js → b.js → a.js confirmed by repository summary.

findings.title: load_config returns None on any exception, caller may not handle
findings.description: Bare `except: pass` returns `None` implicitly for any error (missing file, permission, etc.). Callers expecting a string may crash with AttributeError.
findings.suggestion: Catch specific exceptions (FileNotFoundError, OSError) and either re-raise or return a sentinel value; avoid bare except.
findings.benefit: Prevents silent failures and makes error handling explicit.
findings.risk: Low — callers must be audited for None checks.
